newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Chan urges media to uphold freedom after '97.
newsitem.headline: HK's Chan urges media to uphold freedom after '97.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant, Anson Chan, on Monday urged the territory's media to uphold press freedom after China resumes sovereignty on July 1.
In a speech at a media convention, the Chief Secretary pledged that the government would do its part by protecting press freedom after the British depart at midnight on June 30.

"I urge you all therefore to practise your profession after 1997 as you have always practised it -- continue to write the stories and editorials that deserve to be written, responsibly, objectively but without fear or favour," said Chan.

"The government is doing its share to uphold press freedom but all these efforts will come to nought if those who belong to the profession do not stand up for their own freedom," said Chan, who will remain in her position after the handover.
With the handover just 176 days away, the territory of 6.3 million is worried that its freedoms, particularly those of the media, will be curtailed.

Although China, under Sino-British handover treaties, has promised Hong Kong a high degree of self-rule for the next 50 years, conflicting signals from Chinese officials have alarmed the population in recent months.
Last year, Lu Ping, a top Chinese official on Hong Kong affairs, caused a stir when he said Beijing would not tolerate any advocacy by the press of independence for Taiwan or Hong Kong.
Chan said the preservation of other freedoms would hinge on a strong and independent press after the handover.
"How well you do your job after the transition will to a very large extent decide how well our other freedoms will be protected," she said.
